label: August 1900
atlas_dek: The episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1900 from our dossiers, placed on 1910 county lines and by month (some July events were first reported in August). Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for 86 episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1900. They come from the 153 located events in the August 1900 table, which includes July events first reported in August and three events found while writing the dossiers. We did not write dossiers for 47 events that were plainly out of scope from the table alone (white victims, no race given, no one harmed, earlier years recalled in editorials and lynching tallies) or that repeat another record, and three more belong to earlier months of 1900. Searches covered August papers, plus September papers for more on known episodes.

Twenty-three of the 109 dossiers are set aside. Four are duplicates folded into another record: the beating of Altoona Pullman employees and the West Indian victims’ appeal to the British consul, both part of the New York riot of August 15; the whipping of Walter Brown, ordered by the Cheneyville, Louisiana, committee; and a second record of the August 26 attacks on Black residents of New York’s West Side. The Louis Miller lynching at Bel Air, Maryland, happened in the spring and is held for its month. Eighteen are out of scope. No report gives anyone’s race for the hanging of William Leonard at Canton, Pennsylvania, the siege of a physician’s house at Gilman, Illinois, the drowning of three gamblers at Portageville, Missouri, the Mulat post office, Solomon Anderson at Burlington, or the Red Shirts at Lucama, North Carolina. The victims were not Black in the mobbing of Charles Ives at Norfolk, the threats against Sanford Jacobi at Montgomery, the threats against Lillian Clayton Jewett, a white Boston opponent of lynching, by the Green Turtle Club of New Orleans and the Regents of the White Shield of Birmingham, and the shooting of the Posey brothers at Alexandria. There was no racial motive at Cooper’s Island, Arkansas (killings among Black men), Shellman, Georgia (a Black mob), and in the flogging of Ed Sullivan at Dawson. Talk of a petition against Black soldiers at San Antonio and a threat Perry Watkins imagined at Takoma Park involved no force; Frank Benjamin’s commuted death sentence at Hampton was a legal act; and a “Newark race riot” named in one passing phrase has no report in either press.

Police violence is kept generously: men shot while fleeing, resisting arrest, or escaping a convict gang are all included. Only gunfights over a crime in progress are set aside. Where no report gives the victim’s race, the entry says so.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched Black and white papers. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. Black-press clippings are shown as page images; white-press clippings are page images where we could place them on the scan, otherwise text.

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
